description: A law, maxim or rule of thumb from human systems, filed so the catalog can test whether it transfers to models. The evidence list is what makes it an entry rather than a quotation: each item is a claim in this catalog and a verdict on what that claim says about the transfer.

origin.description: Who said it, where, roughly when, and the human domain it came from.

transfer.description: Why it should or should not apply to models: the mechanism, not the analogy. Goodhart transfers because of optimisation pressure on a proxy, not because models are people.

sources.description: Where the adage itself is stated or named. Evidence about whether it holds for models goes in `evidence`, as claims.

verdict.description: holds: the claim shows the adage applying to models. breaks: it shows the adage failing. narrows: it holds only under a condition the note states.

evidence_search.description: A record of having looked for evidence either way and not found it. Same role as on techniques.
